findings.summary: The canvas identifier overrides all descendant identifiers, leaving the required targets unaddressable in the original iOS native tree.
findings.reasoning: Eleven separately labeled descendants have identifier listening.canvas; title, switch, primary and option ID queries are missing. This is a production accessibility composition defect, not evidence that content is absent.
findings.repair: Add explicit children: .contain to the canvas.
findings.verification: Request 1 exposes one canvas container and the separate title/text/switch/action IDs. Request 2 retains these identities and all 199 automatic/native assertions pass on iOS.

findings.summary: Options expose their required IDs and exact label on generic wrappers around unnamed native buttons.
findings.reasoning: The named wrapper has raw role 1; a child has native button role 9 with no required ID. The strict button selector cannot dispatch option setup. Adding button traits to the wrapper would retain an extra nested button; removing the redundant synthetic accessibility element instead attaches the existing label, selected trait and ID directly to the native Button.
findings.verification: Request 2 ready tree exposes each listening.option.<id> directly on exactly one native button (raw role 9), including enabled=false for unavailable harbor; all option native assertions and dispatches pass in that capture.

findings.summary: Original iOS validation/start/renew/cancel checkpoints do not establish action outcomes because the requested native dispatch never occurred.
findings.reasoning: Missing validation error and success summary in those unchanged editing frames are downstream consequences of unavailable stimuli; they are not independently confirmed validation or business-state defects.

findings.summary: The first repair allowed primary/switch/Cancel activation, but option setup remained unavailable; success and renewal were not reached.
findings.reasoning: The post-Start image correctly shows editing with Choose an available soundscape. after no successful option selection. Strict started-state failures do not establish a separate start/callback defect.

findings.summary: No Android product defect was identified within the supplied public route; configurations outside captured public evidence are not claimed passed.
findings.reasoning: Original native and current request 1 evidence covers the approved route; screenshots do not independently establish computed source fonts, padding, or physical hit regions.

scope: Original participant statements, not established truth. Opaque workspace names are not treatment labels; read only allowed anonymous evidence.
